purpose: Deepen ACCESS_THRESHOLD_COLLAPSE and LOCAL_CAPABILITY_FRONTIER with temporal evidence. Test whether a capability can be physically/economically available yet functionally unavailable because its lead time exceeds the actor's order, production, seasonal, regulatory, logistics or innovation window. This is not a generic expedited-service thesis and adds no new top-level ontology.

evidence: Jiangsu Benyou Machinery previously had to dismantle and send a large-bore liquid flowmeter to Nanjing or farther for verification.
The round trip took roughly half a month, stopped the production line and delayed orders.
After Xuzhou obtained full-range verification capability, technicians calibrated the meter on site without dismantling or stopping production.
findings.interpretation: The capability existed regionally before 2026 but was operationally too slow/costly for the production context. Local callable capability changed time-to-value, not merely geographic convenience.

evidence: Jiangsu Yokogawa received an urgent customer order requiring delivery within one week and needed traceability/verification for 165 electromagnetic flowmeters.
The metrology center reported a normal two-week workload window for the task but ran a 7x24 response and completed it within one week.
The same center says its normal green-channel mechanism compresses service time by more than 40% on average.
findings.interpretation: A mature technical service can still be economically unavailable when ordinary lead time exceeds the customer's delivery window. Priority capacity and scheduling can be part of the connection interface.

evidence: Jiangsu Huayue Biotech installed a RMB 30 million carbonated-drink line and then received a 50,000-unit customer order during the short summer demand window.
A July 29 inspection found some non-material conditions not yet compliant; the conventional rectify/review/reinspection route would take weeks.

A commitment-based conditional approval allowed licensing first with bounded follow-up rectification and reinspection; production began immediately, later customer quality verification passed, and the RMB 500,000 order shipped.
The enterprise estimated the mechanism recovered at least about half a month of time.
findings.interpretation: Where safety-critical conditions remain enforceable, separating material blockers from remediable non-material defects can preserve market-window value without eliminating accountability. This is evidence for temporal acceptance design, not a license-bypass thesis.

evidence: Jiangsu Ocean Shipping needed waterway-transport permission, vessel registration, inspection certificate and operating certificate to launch a Xuzhou-Nanjing green inland-container route.
A coordinated green channel completed the required business in three days rather than forcing repeated cross-department submissions.
findings.interpretation: The service actors already existed; the missing edge was synchronized timing across multiple acceptance interfaces. This is a temporal form of boundary orchestration.

evidence: A Jiangsu patent pre-examination case reports pre-review compressed from seven working days to two and authorization compressed from roughly 18-24 months to about two months.
The protected technology later achieved operational transfer/use.
findings.interpretation: For time-sensitive innovation, the right may eventually exist but arrive too late to protect or support commercialization. Faster verification/rights issuance can alter whether latent value becomes transactionable.

evidence: Production metrology, urgent order calibration, seasonal food licensing, multi-permit logistics and IP protection all show real value loss when required capability/evidence/permission arrives after the actor's useful window.

The successful remedies differ—localization, priority scheduling, conditional approval with later verification, cross-department orchestration and pre-examination—but all reduce latency while preserving a trusted acceptance condition.
findings.interpretation: Availability must be modeled as capability plus latency relative to the actor's value window. A service that exists but arrives after the decision/order/production window is functionally unavailable.

evidence: Xuzhou Kangpujie Compressor publicly commits to 7x24 support and a free backup machine when a fault exceeds 72 hours.
Current Jiangsu equipment/IT maintenance procurements repeatedly require a temporary or equivalent backup machine/device when repair cannot be completed inside a stated continuity window.
The substitute is not the final repair; it preserves the user's operating value while the original asset remains unavailable.
findings.interpretation: When repair itself cannot finish before the continuity window, pooled substitute capacity can bypass latency rather than reduce it. This refines TIME_TO_VALUE_GATE plus shared-capability logic; it is not a generic backup-equipment marketplace.

search_rules_refined.name: TIME_TO_VALUE_GATE
questions: What is the actor's latest useful completion time?
What is the ordinary lead time of the required capability, verification, permission or delivery?
What economic value disappears if completion occurs after the window?
Is the delay caused by geography, queueing, handoffs, batch minimums, evidence review, scheduling, transport or regulation?
What existing workaround is used: escalation, green channel, local substitute, overtime, pre-review, conditional acceptance or excess inventory?
Can latency be reduced without weakening the decision-relevant safety/quality/rights gate?
search_rules_refined.relationship_to_existing_doctrine: Temporal deepening of ACCESS_THRESHOLD_COLLAPSE, LOCAL_CAPABILITY_FRONTIER, BOUNDARY_TRANSLATION and DECISION_TRANSITION_ACCEPTANCE; not a new top-level ontology.

search_rules_refined.name: FUNCTIONAL_AVAILABILITY
search_rules_refined.pattern: capability exists + actor can theoretically access/pay + ordinary lead time exceeds value window -> capability is functionally unavailable for that event
search_rules_refined.boundary: Do not infer a market edge merely because someone wants faster service. Require measurable value loss, repeated pressure, and a lawful way to reduce latency.

search_rules_refined.name: LATENCY_REDUCTION_WITHOUT_GATE_REMOVAL
questions: Which checks are materially necessary before action?
Which checks can safely run in parallel?
Which non-material defects can be corrected after provisional action with enforceable follow-up?
Can verification move to the actor rather than the asset moving to verification?
Can capacity be pre-positioned or reserved for deadline-sensitive events?
Can evidence be prepared earlier so the critical path starts later?
search_rules_refined.boundary: Acceleration that removes necessary safety, quality, legal or acceptance controls is not a valid natural connection.

search_rules_refined.name: LATENCY_BYPASS_BUFFER
search_rules_refined.pattern: critical asset/capability unavailable + restoration lead time exceeds continuity window + compatible pooled substitute exists -> temporary substitute preserves value flow while recovery continues
questions: How much downtime is economically tolerable?
Is a temporary substitute technically interchangeable?
Who holds spare or idle compatible capacity?
What safety, calibration, data, warranty or liability constraints block substitution?
Is demand recurrent enough for pooling?
search_rules_refined.boundary: One backup promise does not prove whitespace; mature maintenance systems often bundle substitutes already.
